01

Overview

What the simulator models

This simulator deals independent hands of 8/5 Bonus Poker from a fresh 52-card deck. It chooses cards to hold using a fixed, ordered 37-rule strategy chart, draws replacement cards, evaluates the final hand, and applies the paytable below.

This is not an AI model. The hold decision is deterministic: rules are checked from first to last, and the first matching rule wins.

A win means any final category with a non-zero paytable return, including Jacks or Better. A final category of Nothing is a loss. Betting ladders react to that win/loss definition.

02

Inputs

Parameter guide

Games per set

The maximum number of hands in each set. A bankroll threshold can stop a set earlier. Range: 1–100,000.

Number of sets

How many independent sessions to run. Total requested hands—games × sets—cannot exceed 1,000,000.

Betting mode

Selects fixed-credit play or one of five credit progressions. Modes 1–5 always begin at 1 credit.

Credits per bet

The number of credits used on every hand in Mode 0. Modes 1–5 ignore this input because the ladder controls credits.

Denomination

The cash value of one credit. The hand’s bet is denomination × credits.

Seed

An optional whole number used to reproduce an experiment. Leave it blank for a fresh random seed.

Starting balance

The bankroll available at the beginning of every set. It must be greater than zero.

Walk-away balance

A set stops after a completed hand reaches or exceeds this target. It must be greater than the starting balance.

Minimum balance

A set stops after a completed hand reaches or falls below this amount. It must be below the starting balance.

03

Credit progression

Betting modes

0

No Ladder

Uses the selected fixed credit on every hand. Previous wins and losses do not change the next bet.

selected credit → selected credit
1

Loss Ladder

Moves up one level after a loss, remains at 5 after further losses, and resets to 1 after any win.

1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5
2

Win Ladder

Moves up one level after a win, remains at 5 after further wins, and resets to 1 after any loss.

1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5
3

D'Alembert Ladder

Moves up one credit after a loss and down one credit after a win, staying within the 1–5 range.

loss +1 · win −1
4

Aggressive Win Ladder

Advances more quickly after wins, remains at 5 after further wins, and resets to 1 after any loss.

1 → 2 → 4 → 5
5

Aggressive Loss Ladder

Advances more quickly after losses, remains at 5 after further losses, and resets to 1 after any win.

1 → 2 → 4 → 5
Important: a betting progression changes bet exposure, volatility, and the probability of reaching a stopping target. It does not change the underlying expected return of a credit wagered.
04

Repeatability

How seeds work

The seed shown in the results is the master seed. For a multi-set experiment, it deterministically generates a different internal seed for each set. Sets therefore do not replay the same sequence.

Master seedSet 1 seedSet 2 seedSet 3 seed
  • Leave Seed blank to generate a new master seed using browser randomness.
  • Reuse the same master seed and identical parameters to reproduce the full browser experiment.
  • Use the same seed across betting modes to make mode comparisons more controlled.
  • The browser and Python simulators use different random-number generators, so the same numeric seed does not produce identical deals between them.
05

Reports

Reading the results

Average games

Mean hands completed per set. This can be lower than requested when bankroll rules stop sets early.

Total bet / returned

Average dollars bet and paid back per set. Return is returned ÷ bet.

Net

Average returned minus average bet. A negative number is an average loss.

Ending bankroll

The final balance for one set or the average final balance across multiple sets.

Credit levels

How often each credit level was used, averaged per set for multi-set runs.

Set outcomes

Counts and rates for reaching the target, minimum, insufficient funds, or the hand limit.

For one set, the chart shows that set’s bankroll after each hand. For multiple sets, it shows the average bankroll at each hand. If a set stops early, its ending balance is carried forward so every later chart point still averages all sets.

07

First match wins

37-rule hold strategy

Starting with Rule 1, hold the first pattern found. “Suited” means all listed cards share a suit. “Unsuited” excludes the suited version. The final rule discards all five cards.

  1. Royal Flush.
  2. Straight Flush.
  3. Four Aces, discarding the kicker.
  4. Any other Four of a Kind, discarding the kicker.
  5. Four suited cards from T–J–Q–K–A.
  6. Full House.
  7. Three Aces.
  8. Flush.
  9. Any other Three of a Kind.
  10. Straight.
  11. Four-card Straight Flush with no gap.
  12. Two Pair.
  13. Four-card Straight Flush with a gap.
  14. Pair of Jacks, Queens, Kings, or Aces.
  15. Three suited cards from T–J–Q–K–A.
  16. Four cards to a Flush.
  17. Any four-card, no-gap Straight from A–2–3–4 through J–Q–K–A, regardless of suits.
  18. Low Pair: 2s through 10s.
  19. Suited 9–T–J.
  20. Suited J–Q.
  21. Suited 8–9–J or 8–T–J.
  22. Suited J–K or Q–K.
  23. Suited J–A, Q–A, or K–A.
  24. 9–J–Q–K, T–J–Q–A, T–J–K–A, or T–Q–K–A.
  25. J–Q–K.
  26. Unsuited J–Q: hold only the Jack.
  27. Suited T–J.
  28. Unsuited J–K or Q–K.
  29. Unsuited J–A, Q–A, or K–A.
  30. Suited T–Q.
  31. Suited T–K.
  32. Single Ace.
  33. Single King.
  34. Single Queen.
  35. Single Jack.
  36. Any three suited cards contained in a five-rank Straight window, allowing up to two gaps—for example, suited 3–5–7.
  37. Discard all cards.
